messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary p99 latency breach detected for model redwood/v7-quant in us-west-2 (traffic: 7% of production).
Metrics snapshot: p50=80ms, p95=410ms (baseline ~120ms), p99=2.1s (baseline ~280ms). Streaming stall rate = 3.6% (normal <0.2%). Routing weight change detected ~10:12:06 UTC.
oncall-bot: Incident severity estimated: S0 -> paging oncall. Link: https://alerts.internal/reports/1909997777
evan.p: seeing it on dashboards too :eyes:  p99 spike starts at 10:12 UTC and correlates with canary weight bump from 5%->7% per deployment logs. Any recent kernel/quant changes shipped with v7?
samir.k: v7-quant included a new fused-attn kernel and a slightly different kv-cache layout. We rolled that yesterday in canary. I can grab logs from the canary hosts.
maria_l: tagging CSMs for top customers who had traffic routed to the canary earlier today. @product-ops-bot can you open postmortem skeleton and notify CSM-runbook?
product-ops-bot: Postmortem created: https://incidents.internal/1909997777/postmortem. Notifying CSMs: enterprise-cust-A, enterprise-cust-B.
ev an.p: small note: streaming stalls are the main customer-visible issue; quick customer impact check: any errors in gateway or timeouts from client side?
samir.k: grabbing logs — running a targeted query.

samir.k: Kibana query I'm running: 
```
index=runtime-logs-*
service=frontend AND model:redwood/v7-quant AND timestamp:[2026-03-10T10:05:00 TO 2026-03-10T10:20:00]
| json latency_ms, stream_stall
| where latency_ms > 500
| sort by timestamp desc
```
Found multiple span traces where stream was open but no tokens emitted for 3-8s. Stack shows process pinned at CUDA memcpy + kernel launch queue.
evan.p: could be kernel scheduling under contention. Can we reduce canary traffic to 0% while we triage? That will limit customer impact.
samir.k: I can change rollout weight via control-plane API. Proposed command: 
```
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.redwood.internal/v1/rollouts/redwood/v7-quant" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"target_percent":0, "reason":"emergency rollback - p99 spike"}'
```
Doing it now.

sre-shift: Please wait 10s and verify metrics after change. I'll watch for error/exception spikes.
samir.k: submitted change, rollout API returned ok, new weight=0% for canary at 10:15:42 UTC.
evan.p: confirming on dashboards — traffic to v7 dropped to 0. Streaming stall rate dropping in the next sample. p99 trending down (2.1s -> 520ms) within two minutes. :thumbsup:

eng-runtime: quick note — when canaries use the fused-attn we changed allocator path; there was also a small change to KV cache sharding. Both could interact under bursty traffic. I'll capture core dumps and kernel traces from the affected hosts.
samir.k: capturing dmesg, nvidia-smi logs, and runtime traces now. Uploading artifacts to /artifacts/1909997777.
maria_l: Customer update draft: "We detected an elevated latency and streaming stall rate affecting a small % of traffic routed to a new canary model version. We rolled back canary traffic and are monitoring improvements; engineers are investigating root cause. We'll follow up in the incident doc." Anyone want to edit?
evan.p: looks good. Add estimated time window: 10:12-10:16 UTC and mention potential short tail for retried requests.
product-ops-bot: Scheduled notification to CSMs sent.

sre-shift: action items so far: 1) rollback canary traffic -> done. 2) capture host/kernel/runtime traces -> in progress. 3) open incident timeline and customer impact -> Maria to own. 4) eng-runtime to triage kernel/kv interaction. 5) if metrics don't recover within 15m, consider draining hosts and repro locally.

eng-runtime: initial hypothesis: under certain input length distributions we flush larger KV pages which increases memcpy latency; fused-attn kernel has slightly higher enqueue overhead causing backlog on CUDA stream. Need to reproduce with similar request shape locally on a test cluster.
samir.k: I see a small error pattern: OOM-protection path triggered briefly on two GPUs (2x minor page faults) — not full OOM but causes a stall while the allocator recovers. I'm attaching the snippet: 
```
[10:12:14] WARN allocator: minor page fault, reclaimed 48MB
[10:12:14] INFO runtime: resuming queue on device gpu-7
[10:12:16] WARN stream: kernel enqueue delay 3124ms
```
That matches the stall windows.
evan.p: can we mitigate without full rollback if we reconfigure kernel to use legacy allocator? Is there runtime flag?

eng-runtime: there is a runtime flag to disable fused-attn optimized path: `--disable-fused-attn`. We can hotflip config for canary hosts, but since we already rolled back traffic to 0% it's lower priority. If rollback had not fixed it we'd toggle that.
samir.k: verifying post-rollback metrics: p95=130ms, p99=290ms, streaming stall rate=0.1% — essentially back to normal baselines.

sre-shift: good recovery. Next steps: eng-runtime to continue root-cause analysis (collect kernel traces, reproduce), samir to correlate host-level memory events with request shapes, maria to complete customer impact and send a brief to CSMs with timeline. Postmortem owner needed.
maria_l: I'll be postmortem owner, will draft and assign to eng-runtime for RCA and to samir for host evidence. ETA for draft: EOD today.
evan.p: handoff to next oncall in 30m — summarize status please.
sre-shift: Handoff summary (to whoever picks oncall):
- Incident: Canary-induced p99 latency spike for redwood/v7-quant, us-west-2.
- Window: 10:12 - 10:16 UTC.
- Impact: brief elevated p99 and increased streaming stalls for ~7% production traffic; rollback to 0% removed the regression.
- Actions taken: rollback via control plane, artifacts collected (/artifacts/1909997777), postmortem created and CSMs notified.
- Owners: Maria (postmortem & customer comms), eng-runtime (RCA), Samir (host logs & traces).

product-ops-bot: Handoff note saved to incident doc.

evan.p: thanks all. If eng-runtime reproduces a deterministic trigger, let's schedule a canary re-run behind darker shadowing only (no live traffic) and add extra telemetry on CUDA enqueue times.

eng-runtime: agreed. We'll attempt to reproduce with longer input lengths and KV page sizes, and will disable fused-attn if needed in a controlled experiment.

sre-shift: closing the active paging loop. All monitoring alerts suppressed for this incident window. If anything regresses we re-open. Oncall handoff to next shift at 11:00 UTC.
maria_l: I'll send final customer follow-up once RCA draft is ready.

oncall-bot: Incident closed (auto): paging status -> resolved. Reference: https://incidents.internal/1909997777
